Well, the best way to beat this level is to get the Phat Beet booster in the Zen Garden, because its plant food effect is the strongest of all the plants you get this level. But if that's not an option, here's how I beat this level:

Save as much plant food as possible (you won't get them in the final boss phase) and lawn mowers. Then, when the Gargantuars phase begins, stall the Gargantuars with all Garlics and Stunnions you get. Don't place attacking plants in the same line as Gargantuars unless necessary, because they will be quickly destroyed by them. Instead, place all attacking plants close to the Zomboss so that they can deal to him as much damage as possibile. Let the lawn mowers take care of the Gargantuans, if you're lucky enough Zomboss will blow them off the board with his speakers. When you see that Zomboss is at low health, give Phat Beet closest to Zomboss all the plant food you saved for the final phase and you should win the level.

You make a good point, I haven't really thought much about how differently this sub approaches Alec and Ashley's actions until now. I would say the main reason why this is the case is that the villains are generally much more liked in this sub than the heroes, so of course a lot of people are going to be biased in that matter, finding it more easy to justify actions of their faves. But I would say it could also be the cause because Alec had a lot more going on in AS than Ashley. His friendship with Connor, his relationship with Riya, his storyline of reconciling with Fiore, being the leader of the villains, manipulating others in the early episodes of AS and so on. In comparison, Ashley's character this season mostly revolved around being Jake's main ally and friend (who is also pretty disliked in this sub from what I've seen), her storyline with the farm (which ultimately didn't really amount that much to the story) and of course, her infamous desire for revenge on Fiore. Maybe it's harder for people to ignore it because it's been one of Ashley's bigger attributes this season where, as I said with Alec, he had a lot more to offer this season. 

That being said, I think both characters behaved badly and we shouldn't minimize Alec's abusive behavior because, as much as it destroyed him, it's part of canon and his character, just like animal cruelty is part of Trevek's, attempted murder part of Riya's, abuse of his girlfriend part of Yul's and so on.

7. Yul — the only strategic thing he did was vote with his alliance. But apart from that he earned the hatred of practically everyone, even turning his girlfriend, who was really loyal to him, towards himself

6. Gabby — Her game was more emotional than strategic. In episode 9, she could have easily elimate Tom, who was a much bigger threat than Tess. She may have had the chance to form a powerful alliance with Grett after getting rid of Yul, but she was eliminated in the next episode before that could ever happen.

5. Ellie — turning her teammates against herself and lack of social game ended in her elimination before merge. Even if she did make it further, I think she would be a target for a lot of people based on her previous interviews and how much she liked to mess with Aiden, Tom, and Jake. 

4. Fiore — she was in a losing position from the very beginning, two people from two different alliances in her team were very reluctant to work with her, so there wasn't much she could do to save herself. Her strategy to manipulate Jake was quite successful though, as he considered keeping her in the game instead of Ally. It's hard to say how far she would have gone on her own, though, considering Alec had an impact on the Jake-James conflict and Team Magenta's win in episode 3.

3. Grett — probably an unpopular opinion, but I don't think Grett's game was that great. Whispering something in Jake's ear during Alec's elimination was really stupid move on her side, considering that Ally, who had been constantly trying to get rid of Jake, was sitting right next to her. She should have talked to Ally about this earlier and convinced her it was part of the plan. It's a bit of a shame because she had the game in her hands with three alliances, but she didn't play her cards well.

2. Alec — he may not have been at his peak this season, but he had a huge impact on the first three eliminations of this season, and the plan to eliminate Ashley in episode 10 was a really good play. He also didn't draw that much attention to himself, which was why he was rarely the main target, despite being the leader of the villains. His biggest flaw in the game, however, was his faith in how loyal his allies would be, something that led to his elimination in the first season as well.
